literal: Virtue having destroyed, unvirtuous things than doing, worse indeed: behind the back having slandered, having acted falsely smiling.
translation: Smiling falsely to someone's face while destroying their reputation behind their back is worse than abandoning virtue and committing evil deeds.
modern: அறத்தை அழித்து பாவங்களைச் செய்வதை விட, ஒருவருக்குப் பின்னால் அவரைப் பற்றி அவதூறு பேசிவிட்டு நேரில் பொய்யாகச் சிரிப்பது மிகவும் தீமையானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet compares two types of wrongdoing to highlight the severity of backbiting. The first line describes a person who abandons virtue and commits evil deeds. The second line states that it is even worse to destroy someone's reputation behind their back and then smile falsely to their face. The repetition of the word 'aḻīi' (having destroyed) powerfully links the destruction of abstract virtue with the destruction of a person's good name, showing that deceitful slander is the greater evil.
